column1: # How many lexemes are still short of their encounter target — a ratchet, not a report.
# Columns: level
# `target` is how many *different* sentences a word of that level must appear in
# before a learner can be expected to know it. Research on vocabulary acquisition
# puts durable learning at roughly 8–12 encounters in varied contexts (Nation);
# 6 for A1 and 4 for A2 are the thresholds §5 of the dataset-expansion brief set,
# deliberately below the research figure because the scheduler re-shows items too.
# `short` is how many lexemes are currently below it. It is a **ceiling that only
# comes down**: the build fails if the real number is higher, which catches the
# regression this file exists to prevent — adding vocabulary faster than the
# sentences that exemplify it. Two content passes in this repository have done
# exactly that, and the coverage report printed a number nobody had to act on.
# The build also fails when the real number is *lower*, which is the half that
# makes it a ratchet rather than a limit. Improving recycling and leaving the
# ceiling where it was would hand the next pass back the room this one earned.
# So a pass that helps ends with an edit here, and the gain is locked in. This is
# the same bidirectional check `pack.tsv` applies to the item count, for the same
# reason: a number that can only be wrong in the safe direction goes stale.
# **Numerals are not counted here.** They are a generated system rather than
# vocabulary met in reading: `spellCardinal` composes any number, so 1042 is
# askable while existing in no sentence, and the numeral drill is how a learner
# meets `novecientos` — not by finding it in four different texts. The coverage
# report above already counts them apart for the same reason. Measured rather than
# assumed: closing the eight hundreds against a target of four would take
# twenty-four more sentences, every one a variation on "X cost N hundred euros",
# and padding a recycling target is how the target stops meaning anything.
# One word can never reach the target and it is not neglect: `menudo` exists only
# inside `a menudo`, a multiword lemma `tokenise` cannot reach (§3.4 of the
# expansion brief). `0` is therefore the goal for A1 and `1` for A2.
# Run `npm run build:data` to learn the current figures; it prints them either way.
# The long-run goal is `0` on both rows. At 5.4 linked words per sentence that is
# roughly 358 more sentences, and only if every one is built from words that are
# already short — see §3.1 of the brief for why writing them as passages is the
# only approach that has ever worked here.
a1
column4: Two coverage passes added one-encounter words as fast as they fixed them

column1: a2
column4: Met. The one left is menudo, unreachable inside the multiword a menudo
